assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only sayonara-lara:lara@anime#reviewed-literary-monograph, the active_provisional monograph SYL_LARA_MONOGRAPH.md (generation V1_JP_AUDITED, version 1.1) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Sayonara Lara television anime E01-E12 and its six-month coda through aligned Japanese captions and full static images, without direct audio or continuous video. The project's episode readings, ledgers, relationship and specialist studies and other monographs are not curated on this subject and were not used; the claim IDs the monograph cites serve only as locators. The monograph's active_provisional status and its own readiness statements are inputs, not conclusions. The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: E01-E12 and the six-month coda, in five developmental boundaries (E01-E02, E03-E05, E06-E08, E09-E11, E12 with the coda) with scene and timestamp locators at the load-bearing turns. Knowledge gates split states inside those boundaries: the E08 foaming disclosure, whether Luca has heard the deadline in E09, the E11 history and the E12 correction at 14:59-16:27. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: memories placed earlier, such as the childhood ring ceremony, belong to her at every later state. Nothing after the train is covered.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: A governing account (curiosity about humans that predates the prince; inherited guilt that makes her life negotiable; agency as wanting the world without a sovereign's or a witch's test) and a condition table that names which motive becomes salient and which tactic follows: novel safe practice (approach and overcommit before the norm), a burdened friend or household (withdraw or repay; E03 departure, E05 labor, E08 note), danger to a loved person from her heart or blade (warn, distance, imagine self-erasure; E07, E10-E12), a deadline nobody else knows about (compress time; E09), and authority claiming her body or love (internalize guilt, compare testimony, then refuse a victim; E10-E12). Its reasoning model predicts her mistakes: she generalizes too fast from one salient example (E05 Makoto's job-as-romance formula, E05 01:37-10:38; E09 dating formula, S05-S13), and her unilateral protective withdrawal takes the other person's voice away (E03, E08, E10). It says what revises her (concrete correction, a second account from the other person, E07 S05-S15), so B. Not A: the monograph says her desires form no fixed hierarchy, and when she fears causing lethal harm, withdrawal or self-erasure and approach stay live alternatives. Its predictions are retrospective conditional readings in 23 KB. Not C: the conditions, knowledge gates and failure cases make up a discriminating account, not interpretation alone.

Five developmental boundaries (E01-E02, E03-E05, E06-E08, E09-E11, E12 with the six-month coda), each stating what she can newly do or say and what she still cannot command, plus located knowledge gates: the E08 disclosure of the foaming risk, whether Luca has heard the deadline (E09), and the E11 history of Rowan and Grace. The E12 correction from self-erasure to wanting tomorrow is located at 14:59-16:27. So B. Not A: three boundaries group several episodes. Inside them only the E05 job sequence, the E07 Luca bridge and the E08 disclosure are located finely. The six months before the train are elided. Not C: the states change conditions on behavior, not only labels.

Located textual language is limited to a few signature lines (もっと触れないと and もっと知らないと 人間のことを in E03, 少なくとも今日は in E05, the repeated ちがう before よみがえってよかった in E12, 私と生きたい, このキズが私) and pragmatic habits: she makes declarations before the other person can take them in, asks literal questions, and says she is fine until someone asks about her face (E08). There is no register analysis (self-reference, politeness level, sentence endings), and audio was not inspected. The row's SPEECH dimension concerns textual language only. So D. Not C: the evidence locates what she says at turning points and how she pushes a declaration, but not a register to constrain wording. Not E: the pragmatic habits recur across E03-E12 with located counterexamples.

The section on ordinary affect gives a located pattern for unfamiliar benign environments: notice a striking affordance or something edible or aesthetic, ask to take part, then need correction about the labor and permission behind it. Located in the cake shop and bakery (E05 03:35-10:38), the camera and portrait (E07 S05-S09), the custard cake (E08 S16), the point card and lost ring (E02 11:24-16:27), and repeated job applications after failed interviews (E05 02:54-05:41). So C. Not B: the sample is mostly first encounters and work. Routine life in the Otsu home after familiarity, school, and the independent residence after the coda are thin or unshown, and the monograph says no universal social style is established. Not D: the pattern is stated and located in more than one setting.

An interlocutor table gives, for Mari and the Otsu home, Luca, Grace/Gon, Lisa, Rowan with the court and the original prince, and coworkers, peers and strangers, what Lara seeks, her characteristic response, and a limit or counterexample. Mari: following, learning through the household, misreading limits as expulsion, hidden departures (E03, E08), forbidding rescue (E10), corrected by Mari's explicit friendship, fear and loneliness. Luca: laughing at his art, refusing contact, hearing his changed account, asking to be lovers, then pressing past his pace under an undisclosed deadline (E07 S08-S15, E09 S12-S13, E12 S12). So B. Not A: the Grace, Lisa and Rowan rows are compact, and the terms with Mari after the coda are unsettled. Not C: each sampled relationship changes the predicted response, and the table states how.

Interior states are located at turning points: fear of death admitted to Mari (E08 08:20-10:01), the self-erasure verdict and its own-words revision (E12 14:59-16:27), the meaning of the ring when it is lost (E02), and guilt taken from Grace's blame and Rowan's duty. The monograph explains how guilt makes her life feel negotiable and what Mari's objection changes. So C. Not B: between those peaks interior state is inferred from conduct in a caption and static-image lane, without audio affect, and the monograph doesn't follow it continuously. Not D: the decisive inner turns are located and explained.

Located conflict behavior with each opponent: early Rowan (doubt ranked as sin; she resists by going to the prince but lacks resources), Grace's proposal to use Mari (refused in E03, through unilateral departure), Lisa's claim that no mermaid-human love can work (resists, joins her under E08 medical pressure, then turns back), Luca's boundary (accepts lover status but pushes physical pace, E09), and the E10-E12 blade command (refuses Rowan's requested blood and her own proposed self-removal). The authority row of the condition table gives a chronology: internalize guilt, compare rival testimony, refuse a victim while keeping family concern. So B. Not A: physical conflict and strike choreography are outside the lane, and the monograph abstains where the severity of the blade decides. Not C: the account predicts her conflict tactics by opponent and state, including the costly ones.

Located positions on three kinds of question: using a host instrumentally (refused in E03 against Grace's proposal), sacrificing a beloved to restore the family (refused in E10-E12, without dropping family concern), and her own erasure as a way to spare others (offered, then rejected in her own words in E12). The monograph states the strongest counteraccount (others pay the costs of her leaving) and keeps it open. So C. Not B: it leaves how she weighs duty to the polity against her own life in a new case explicitly unsettled ('agency as an ongoing responsibility'), and it doesn't give a deliberation procedure beyond the located refusals. Not D: the refusals are located and conditioned on what she knows.

Located delight and laughter: she laughs at Luca's portrait because its colors don't resemble a likeness (E07), writes an overblown slogan that she could die for cake (E05), and takes pleasure in the peach tart and the custard cake. The comedy in these scenes is mostly others' reactions to her literalism, and the monograph doesn't say when or why she starts play. So D. Not C: there is no account of her play to predict from. Not E: the delight is located in more than one episode.

One active_provisional monograph (generation V1_JP_AUDITED, version 1.1, 22,900 bytes) covers E01-E12 and the six-month coda in the aligned Japanese caption and full static-image lane, with timestamp and scene locators. Direct audio and continuous motion are uninspected (SYL-D0001-D0003). The project ledgers whose claim IDs the monograph cites are not curated on this subject and were not used. So C. Not B: a whole performance channel is absent, and the evidence is one compact item. Not D: narrative coverage is complete for the declared lane.

Affirmative limits and disconfirmers: four disconfirmers for 'Lara becomes independent' (family light still bound to a polity, medicine and lifespan unsolved, six months elided with no account of rent or support, Mari's explicit loneliness) and four for 'selfish runaway' (real work, an offered future dialogue with the court, fear of harming loved people, refusal to take a victim). Also: 'free spirit' predicts none of her costly reversals; Luca's E09 boundary is information asymmetry, not proof that she ignores refusals; the first attraction does not establish exclusive heterosexuality or make Mari a substitute romance; the train is not a certificate of self-sufficiency. So B. Not A: the explicit abstentions (blade severity, survival, medicine schedule, housing, consent) are stated but not tested. Not C: these are affirmative, located limits, not silence.

Episode-level boundaries, scene and timestamp locators at the load-bearing turns (E01 08:21-08:53, E03 07:45-08:04, E05 01:37-10:38 and 17:24-18:41, E08 08:20-10:01, E12 14:22-16:27 and 14:59-16:27), and explicit knowledge conditions (before and after the E08 foaming disclosure, whether the deadline is disclosed, before and after the E11 history). So B. Not A: several boundaries group episodes, and the coda compresses six months. Not C: predictions are tied to what she knows at a located point.

scenario_readiness.note: The evidence locates a few signature lines and pragmatic habits (early declarations, literal questions, 'fine' until asked) but no register, and audio was not inspected. Generated lines would be constrained in what she declares or asks, not in how she says it, which is too little for dialogue use. Speech-act content is available as behavioral description under CROSS_SCENARIO.

conditions: Chronology is one named state from cross_scenario_scope; knowledge of the foaming risk, of the deadline and of the E11 history follows that state, and memories placed earlier belong to her throughout.

The situation is one the condition table samples: novel safe human practice, a burdened friend or household, danger to a loved person from her heart or blade, a deadline nobody else knows, or authority claiming her body or love.

The interlocutor is Mari, Luca, Grace or Gon, Lisa or Rowan as located, or a coworker, peer or stranger in a first-contact setting. A comparable unsampled acquaintance is a separate, lower-confidence condition handled without invented history.
When she fears causing lethal harm, withdrawal or self-erasure and approach are output as alternatives, conditioned on whether the other person has answered or objected, never resolved.

Output abstains where the blade's severity, bodily survival, the medicine schedule, unshown housing or the other person's consent would decide the answer, and is behavioral description, not quoted dialogue.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named monograph state: E01-E02, E03-E05, E06-E08 split at the E08 foaming disclosure, E09-E11 split at whether Luca has heard the deadline and at the E11 history, E12 before or after the 14:59-16:27 correction, or post-coda (default). Earlier states never import later knowledge or the E12 correction.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Mari as household guide, friend and holder of an explicit shared-life wish; Luca as recognized suitor, then lover, then former partner after E12; Grace or Gon, Lisa and Rowan at their located positions; coworkers, school peers and strangers only as encountered in first-contact settings. A comparable unsampled acquaintance is a separate, lower-confidence condition, and an unsampled intimate is outside scope.
setting_constraints: The Otsu home, shops, the bakery workplace, school, a date or gallery, the sea and court as shown
A benign novel human practice, a burden on a host, danger to a loved person, an undisclosed deadline, or an authority claiming her body or love
No resolution of the blade's future severity, her long-term survival, the medicine schedule, independent housing or rent, or a mutually agreed future with Mari
No audio, voice or physical-choreography claims

scenario_readiness.note: Readiness depends on one named state, a sampled relationship and one of the five condition-table situations. The high-stakes withdraw-or-approach fork and every abstention the monograph names stay open.

conditions: The setting is a first encounter with a benign human practice (shop, bakery work, phone, camera, art, food) or the Otsu household as sampled.
Output follows the located pattern: notice, ask, overcommit, need correction, then real participation; repeated exposure is not permanent incomprehension.
Familiar daily routine, the independent residence after the coda and a universal social style are outside scope.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported for unfamiliar benign settings like those sampled: she notices an affordance, asks to take part, overcommits, and learns from concrete correction.

conditions: The question is instrumental use of a host, sacrifice of a beloved for the family or polity, or her own erasure to spare others.
Chronology follows the authority row: guilt internalized early, rival testimony compared by E11, a victim refused from E10-E12, self-erasure rejected only after the E12 correction.
Weighing duty to the court against her own life in an unprecedented case is output as open, with the costs to others kept live.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported only for the three located kinds of question; how she weighs family duty against her own life in a new case stays open.

conditions: With Luca: the state is named (E07 recognition, E09 lover request with or without the deadline disclosed, or after the E12 report of dating and breakup); her pressure on pace follows an undisclosed clock and is not a general disregard for refusal.
With Mari: 私と生きたい is strong person-directed language beside a chosen departure; romance, exclusivity and a mutually agreed future are not established and are output as open.
The first attraction to the original prince establishes no exclusive orientation and makes no later partner a substitute.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported for the sampled Luca arc and, without a romance model, for Mari's person-directed shared-life wish.

conditions: The setting is applying for or doing entry-level shop or food work as in E05: failed interviews, a form filled in with help, dishwashing before pastry, completing subordinate tasks well enough to help, joining a revised peach tart.
Royal duty and any vocation after the coda are outside scope; her enjoyment is 'at least today', not a lifelong vocation.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported narrowly for entry-level service work like the E05 bakery.

known_limits.statement: The monograph is bound to the aligned Japanese caption and full static-image lane. It makes no claims about pitch, delivery, nonverbal sound, continuous motion or strike choreography (SYL-D0001-D0003).

When she fears her heart or blade could kill a loved person, E07 and E10 withdrawal and E12 self-erasure stay live alternatives to her E08 and E12 approach. The monograph abstains where the blade's future severity, bodily survival, the medicine schedule, unshown housing or the other person's consent would decide.

The train follows a six-month gap with no account of rent, everyday support or practical terms of return. Long-term survival, self-sufficiency and an agreed future with Mari are not established, and Mari's loneliness stays active.

The monograph calls its predictions retrospective conditional readings of known episodes, not a validated prospective behavior model; no held-out or prospective test exists. This limits confidence, not the tier.
No analysis of self-reference, politeness level or sentence endings, and only a few quoted lines, so there is nothing to constrain generated wording.
With coworkers, peers and strangers she is shown mainly in first encounters. The monograph says the evidence does not establish a universal social style across unshown settings.
The SYL-C, R, L, F, W and D claim IDs the monograph cites point to project ledgers that are not curated on this subject. They serve here as locators only and were not read as evidence.
